To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) DeepER outperforms NER in answering questions about entities, (2) DeepER is able to find answers to questions that are not answered by NER, (3) the performance of DeepER can be improved by increasing the size of its entity library, (4) the performance of the DeepER system is comparable to that of NER, and (5) the performance of RAFAEL is comparable to that reported in the literature for other languages.
DeepER approach outperforms NER-based solutions in the case of open-domain factoid questions, but it is still far away from the state-of-the-art in this area of natural language processing.

DeepER is a novel, efficient and effective approach to the task of entity recognition, and that RAFAEL, a question answering system based on DeepER, is a state-of-the-art open-domain factoid QA system for Polish.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (1) the design of an entity library, (2) the design of a DeepER system, (3) the design of the RAFAEL question answering system, and (4) the evaluation of DeepER on a set of questions from a quiz show.
the development of an entity recognition system, which can be used in a question answering system.
the following aspects of question answering systems: entity recognition, question answering evaluation, and a new entity library for Polish.

the DeepER technique, in the case of RAFAEL, outperforms the traditional NER approach by 5.7% in terms of F-measure.
RAFAEL is able to provide a high quality of answers, and DeepER approach is able to provide answers to questions that are not possible to answer with a traditional NER approach.
the presented system, RAFAEL (Rafał), is a competitive and effective open-domain question answering system for the Polish language.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in terms of precision, DeepER is comparable to NER, while in terms of recall it is significantly better.
DeepER, in combination with the NER approach, allows for a more complete and accurate entity recognition, and therefore, a more precise answer to the questions.
DeepER, as a new entity recognition technique, outperformed the NER approach, especially for the more difficult questions, which require answers beyond the traditional named entity types.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DeepER approach can significantly improve a question answering system performance, as well as its ability to answer a wider range of questions.
DeepER can be successfully applied to a variety of languages and domains.
a deep entity recognition approach is a valuable addition to the arsenal of tools that help to answer questions in open domain question answering systems.
